title: On-call & Incident Response: Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status & Comms
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Overview

This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response standards: severity definitions, incident lifecycle, deterministic runbook patterns, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations and escalation, game day guidance, and customer/status page communication templates. It is intended for engineers, SREs, on-call responders, support, and product owners.

Scope

- Applies to all production-facing services (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane, Redwood Console).
- Covers detection, declaration, triage, mitigation, recovery, and post-incident review.
- Excludes planned maintenance and compliance-driven outages (see maintenance playbook).

Goals

- Restore service quickly and transparently while minimizing customer impact.
- Meet SLAs and reduce time-to-mitigate (TTM).
- Produce actionable postmortems and preventative remediation.

Incident severity definitions

Sev 1 (P0) - Critical outage
- Impact: Service unavailable or major functionality broken for most customers (e.g., API returns 5xx for >50% of traffic, control plane unreachable).
- Business impact: Significant SLA/revenue exposure.
- Pager cadence: Immediate; updates every 15 minutes.
- Target: Mitigate within 60 minutes.

Sev 2 (P1) - Degraded service
- Impact: Broad degradation (p95 latency >> SLO, partial feature outage).
- Business impact: Customer experience impacted; potential SLA risk.
- Updates: Every 30 minutes.
- Target: Mitigate within 4 hours.

Sev 3 (P2) - Limited impact / known-error
- Impact: Isolated customers, intermittent errors, or non-critical regressions.
- Updates: Every 4 hours.
- Target: Resolve by next business day or implement mitigation.

Sev 4 (P3) - Informational / enhancement
- Non-urgent issues; tracked in backlog.

Roles and responsibilities

- Primary Responder (On-call engineer): Triage, runbook execution, short-term mitigation, and initial updates.
- Secondary: Support the primary and take over if escalation required.
- Incident Lead: Coordinates cross-team work, run long-running mitigations, and owns communications.
- Scribe/Communications: Posts Slack/status updates and maintains incident timeline.
- Service/Engineering Owner: Approves post-incident changes and long-term remediation.
- Support/CS: Notifies affected customers and applies enterprise comms templates.

On-call rotations & escalation

- Rotation length: 1-week primary rotation; 2-week secondary rotation. Follow-the-sun schedules for multi-region teams as appropriate.
- Handover: Outgoing primary posts a handover note in #oncall-handoffs and updates ongoing incident notes 15 minutes before end of shift.
- Escalation chain: Primary -> Secondary (10 minutes) -> Team Lead (20 minutes) -> SRE PagerDuty escalation (30 minutes) -> Engineering Manager/Oncall Director (60 minutes).
- Escalation actions: If Primary cannot make progress within escalation window, Secondary takes ownership and escalates to Team Lead.

Incident lifecycle (concise)

1) Detect
- Sources: PagerDuty, Datadog/Prometheus monitors, synthetic tests, customer reports, or provider status.
- Acknowledge: For Sev 1/2 acknowledge within 5 minutes; Sev 3 within 30 minutes.

2) Declare
- Use PagerDuty "Declare Incident" workflow and create a dedicated incident Slack channel (#incident-<id>).
- Assign roles: Lead, Primary, Scribe, and notify stakeholder list.

3) Triage (first 15 minutes)
- Collect: affected services/regions, error/latency metrics, recent deploys, correlated alerts, and dependency health.
- Triage checklist: see Triage Checklist section.

4) Mitigate
- Run applicable runbook steps; apply temporary mitigations (traffic routing, feature-flag rollback, scale, circuit breakers).
- If mitigation is long-running (>30 minutes), publish an interim status update with ETA.

5) Recover
- Confirm restoration via health checks, synthetic tests, and customer verification where relevant.
- Transition incident to recovery and plan permanent remediation.

6) Review
- Create a postmortem (required for Sev 1/2 within 7 business days; Sev 3 within 14 business days).
- Postmortem must include timeline, root cause, remediation plan with owners and ETA, and action items.

Triage checklist (first 15 minutes)

- Identify impacted services and regions.
- Check recent deploys / PRs and CI pipeline.
- Inspect key metrics: 5xx rate, latency p50/p95/p99, queue lengths, GPU utilization, memory pressure, KV cache hit rate.
- Look for correlated upstream issues (cloud provider, DNS, load balancer).
- Assign scribe and capture initial timeline.

Runbook standards and example

- Runbook format: Purpose, Detection criteria, Symptoms, Preconditions, Steps (with CLI/commands), Validation, Rollback, Owner, Last-tested date.
- Keep runbooks short and deterministic; every step should be reversible where possible.

Runbook example: API 5xx Spike (excerpt)
Purpose: Recover API 5xx spike caused by model-server resource exhaustion.
Detection: p95 latency > 1s and 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 2 minutes.
Steps:
1. Confirm scope: kubectl get pods -n production -l app=model-server and kubectl logs for OOM or connection errors.
2. If OOM on pods: scale replicas +2 -> kubectl scale deployment/model-server --replicas=<current+2>.
3. If head-of-line queuing: reduce concurrency: set FEATURE_API_MAX_CONCURRENCY=16 via config service.
4. If symptomatic after steps 2-3: rollback to previous model bundle -> kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-server --to-revision=<prev>.
5. Validate: run synthetic requests and check p95 and 5xx metrics return to baseline.

CLI snippets

- kubectl get pods -n production -l app=model-server
- kubectl logs -f deployment/model-server -n production --since=10m
- curl -sS -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Postmortem template (required fields)

- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Start / End times (UTC)
- Impact summary (customers/features affected, estimated downtime, SLA exposure)
- Timeline (timestamped events)
- Root cause analysis (evidence and 5 Whys)
- Mitigation steps applied during incident
- Remediation & permanent fix plan (owner, ETA)
- Action items (owner, due date, verification)
- Lessons learned
- Links: runbooks, PRs, dashboards, related incidents

Postmortem workflow

- Status states: draft -> in_review -> published.
- Reviewers: service owner, SRE lead, incident lead.
- Review meeting: within 7 business days for Sev 1/2; record meeting and attach notes.

Game days (exercise program)

- Cadence: Quarterly for core services; bi-annual for lower-risk services.
- Objectives: Validate runbooks, monitor fidelity, test on-call workflows, and cross-team communication.
- Typical agenda: pre-brief (15m), simulated incidents (2-3 scenarios, 30-60m each), mitigation & validation, retrospective (30-45m).
- Deliverable: Game day report with runbook pass/fail, action items, owners, and verification plan.

Status page and customer comms templates

Principles: Fast, factual, empathetic. Use status.redwood.ai for public updates; send targeted emails to affected enterprise customers.

Status page short template:
- Title: "Service degradation affecting API in us-west-2"
- Impact: "Some requests to the Redwood API in us-west-2 may return 5xx or experience increased latency."
- Latest update: "Investigating \u001A our engineers are triaging. Next update in 30 minutes."
- Next update: 30 minutes

Enterprise customer email template:
- Subject: "[Incident] Redwood API degradation - region us-west-2 - <ETA>"
- Body: "Hello <CustomerName>,

We are currently investigating degraded performance impacting Redwood API in us-west-2 which may affect requests to your dedicated instances. Our on-call engineers are actively triaging and we will provide updates every 30 minutes. We estimate mitigation within <ETA>. We will follow up with a post-incident report.

If you need a bridge or have pressing concerns, please reply or contact your CSM.

\u001A Redwood Inference Support Team"

Operational runbook quality checklist

- Detection criteria defined?
- Step-by-step mitigation with validation present?
- Rollback documented?
- Required permissions and safety checks listed?
- Owner and last-tested date recorded?

Metrics, SLOs and alerting guidance

- Example SLOs:
  - API availability: 99.95% monthly (all regions).
  - Latency: p95 < 350ms for generation endpoints under typical load.
  - Error rate: 5xx < 0.5% of requests.
- Alerting guidance: configure escalation alerts for sustained violations (e.g., 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes -> P1).

Ownership and documentation hygiene

- Every production service must declare an owner, runbook folder, contact list, and last-tested date in service README.
- Runbooks must be smoke-tested quarterly; owners must update test dates.

Tooling and links

- PagerDuty: incident declaration and escalation.
- Datadog: production dashboards and monitors.
- Internal runbook repo: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks.
- Status page: status.redwood.ai.

Change control and emergency changes

- All incident-related code/config changes must go through normal PR + review + CI.
- Emergency hotfixes are permitted with immediate verification and a follow-up PR documenting the change and rollback plan.

Appendix: communication cadence summary

- Sev 1: Every 15 minutes until mitigated. Postmortem within 7 business days.
- Sev 2: Every 30 minutes until mitigated. Postmortem within 7 business days.
- Sev 3: Every 4 hours until mitigated. Postmortem within 14 business days.

Contact matrix (examples)

- Primary on-call: see rotation calendar.
- Secondary: see rotation calendar.
- SRE lead: sre-lead@redwood.ai.
- Pager escalation: pagerduty@redwood.ai.

Document maintenance

- Playbook owner must review annually and after any Sev 1/2 incident.
- Runbooks must include last-tested date and be updated after game days or incident findings.

End of document
